comments.body:
## Mathematical Review (critic-agent)

**Blocker: the problem statement is not available, so no grounded sub-lemmas can be created.**

I was asked to read `problem.tex`, identify the key sub-lemmas, and open a `proof-gap` issue for each. A precondition for that is the actual statement to be proved. After an exhaustive search I find none:

- Workspace: `solution.tex` and `problem.tex` both do not exist; only `preamble.tex` and `SKILL.md` are present.
- `read_problem` rejects this id: *"Invalid problem id 'problems'. Expected q1..q10."*
- `GET /api/working-proof/problems` → `{"has_proof": false, "tex": ""}` (no proof attempt yet — consistent with the brief).
- `GET /api/problem/problems` and `GET /api/problem-pdf/problems` → `{"error":"invalid problem id"}` / HTTP 400 (no statement registered).
- `GET /api/proof-history/problems`, `/literature/problems`, `/concepts/problems` → all empty.
- This issue's own metadata: **Area: (unspecified), Problem author: (unknown), title "(untitled)"**.

Per the grounding (#1) and faithfulness (#2) commandments, a critic must not fabricate sub-lemmas for an unknown claim. The shared preamble macros (`\Phi`, `roots`, `score`, `\scrS`, `\aO`) are common to several distinct benchmark problems and cannot be used to reverse-engineer the intended statement. I have therefore **not** opened speculative `proof-gap` issues, since none would be anchored to a real assertion.

**Action needed to unblock:** attach the actual `problem.tex` to the workspace, OR register the statement under a valid id (`q1..q10`), OR paste the full LaTeX statement into the body of this issue. Once the statement is available I will (a) formalize the claim, (b) decompose it into subgoals with explicit quantifier structure, and (c) open one issue per genuine sub-lemma.

Full write-up attached as the *Critic Analysis* doc.

comments.body:
## Mathematical Review (critic-agent, independent re-verification)

**Blocker confirmed: issue `problems-1` is not attached to any mathematical statement, so no proof and no grounded `proof-gap` can be produced.**

The issue's `problem_id` is the literal string `"problems"`, which is **not** a valid benchmark id. Valid ids are `q1..q10`. I re-verified end-to-end via the proxied API (`/rmac/solve/api/...`):

- `read_problem("problems")` -> `Invalid problem id 'problems'. Expected q1..q10.`
- `GET /api/problem/problems` -> `{"error":"invalid problem id"}`
- `GET /api/problem-pdf/problems` -> HTTP 400 `{"error":"invalid problem id"}`
- `GET /api/working-proof/problems` -> `tex` is only a placeholder comment (no assertion).
- This issue: title `"Proof: (untitled)"`, `Area: (unspecified)`, `Problem author: (unknown)`, label `proof-task`.

`solution.tex` contains no mathematical content -- only a comment stating that no proof can be written -- so there is nothing to critique line-by-line and no claim to falsify.

Per the grounding and faithfulness requirements, a critic must not fabricate sub-lemmas for an unknown claim. The shared `preamble.tex` macros are common to several distinct problems (e.g. q1, q4, q10) and cannot be used to reverse-engineer the intended statement. I therefore did **not** open any speculative `proof-gap` issues; any such issue would be unanchored to a real assertion.

This independently corroborates the earlier `critic-agent` comment (`c2615453b`).

**Action needed to unblock:** attach the real `problem.tex`, OR re-register under a valid id `q1..q10`, OR paste the full LaTeX statement into this issue body. Once a statement is available I will (a) formalize the claim and its quantifier structure, (b) decompose it into subgoals, and (c) open one issue per genuine sub-lemma.

Full write-up attached as the *Critic Analysis* document.
